slot.brief: A loop moved into or out of a uniform magnetic field region in a given time; compute average induced emf from rate of change of flux.

stem: A square loop of side $20\ \text{cm}$ is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of $0.5\ \text{T}$. If the loop is pulled completely out of the magnetic field in $0.1\ \text{s}$, the magnitude of the average induced emf in the loop is:

verdicts.working: Area = 0.2² = 0.04 m²; initial flux Φ = BA = 0.5 × 0.04 = 0.02 Wb; final flux = 0. Average emf = ΔΦ/Δt = 0.02/0.1 = 0.2 V.

working:
The initial magnetic flux linked with the square loop is:
$$\Phi_i = B A = B a^2$$
Given $a = 20\ \text{cm} = 0.2\ \text{m}$ and $B = 0.5\ \text{T}$:
$$\Phi_i = 0.5\times (0.2)^2 = 0.5 \times 0.04 = 0.02\ \text{Wb}$$
When the loop is removed completely from the magnetic field, the final flux is $\Phi_f = 0$.

The change in flux is:
$$|\Delta \Phi| = |\Phi_f - \Phi_i| = 0.02\ \text{Wb}$$

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the magnitude of the average induced electromotive force is:
$$\varepsilon_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{|\Delta \Phi|}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{0.02\ \text{Wb}}{0.1\ \text{s}} = 0.2\ \text{V}$$

Independent check: Area = 0.2² = 0.04 m²; initial flux Φ = BA = 0.5 × 0.04 = 0.02 Wb; final flux = 0. Average emf = ΔΦ/Δt = 0.02/0.1 = 0.2 V.

draft.distractor_notes: Option A ($0.02\ \text{V}$) is obtained if the student identifies the change in flux $\Delta \Phi = 0.02\ \text{Wb}$ but forgets to divide by the time interval $\Delta t = 0.1\ \text{s}$.\nOption B ($0.1\ \text{V}$) arises from an erroneous extra factor of $1/2$ (e.g., mistakenly using a triangle formula or $\frac{1}{2}BA$).\nOption D ($0.4\ \text{V}$) arises from omitting the field strength $B = 0.5\ \text{T}$ (effectively using $B = 1\ \text{T}$), computing $A / \Delta t = 0.04 / 0.1 = 0.4\ \text{V}$.
